findings.title: Base image uses :latest tag
findings.description: Pinning :latest (or omitting the tag, which implies :latest) makes builds non-reproducible and can silently pull a new, vulnerable image. Pin an explicit version tag or digest.

evidence.expected: pinned version tag (e.g. ubuntu:22.04) or digest

findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: Container runs as root
findings.description: Without a USER directive the container runs as root; an explicit USER root (or 0) is the same risk. A container breakout then yields host root. Switch to a non-root user.
findings.remediation: Enable MFA on the account and restrict root usage. Create individual IAM users or federate via SSO, attach least-privilege policies, and never use root for daily operations.

findings.title: Secret in ENV directive
findings.description: ENV values are baked into the image layers and visible to anyone who can pull the image (docker history, inspect). Inject secrets at runtime instead. The secret value is never shown in findings.

evidence.expected: inject secrets at runtime (build args with --secret, runtime env, secret mounts)

findings.remediation: Remove the hardcoded secret immediately and rotate it. Store secrets in AWS Secrets Manager or SSM Parameter Store (SecureString) and reference them via data sources. Never commit secrets to version control — scan history with gitleaks if the value was ever committed.

findings.title: ADD used instead of COPY
findings.description: ADD fetches remote URLs and auto-extracts archives, which can pull untrusted content into the image. Prefer COPY for local files.
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: No HEALTHCHECK directive
findings.description: Without a HEALTHCHECK the orchestrator cannot tell a wedged container from a healthy one, delaying restarts and hiding compromise-induced hangs.
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: apt-get install without --no-install-recommends
findings.description: Installing recommended packages bloats the image with unneeded software, enlarging the attack surface. Pass --no-install-recommends to apt-get install.
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: apt-get update without cache cleanup
findings.description: apt-get update leaves package lists in the image layer. Remove /var/lib/apt/lists/* in the same RUN to keep layers lean.

evidence.expected: clean package lists in the same RUN layer

findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: No WORKDIR directive
findings.description: Without WORKDIR the build and the container run from /, so relative paths and stray files land in the filesystem root. Set an explicit WORKDIR for the application.
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: No maintainer label
findings.description: Images without ownership metadata are harder to triage when a vulnerability is found. Add LABEL maintainer= or org.opencontainers.image.authors.
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: No STOPSIGNAL directive
findings.description: Without STOPSIGNAL the container gets SIGTERM, which apps that only handle SIGINT (or expect another signal) ignore until the orchestrator SIGKILLs them, risking data loss. Declare the signal your app handles for graceful shutdown.
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: Full OS base image
findings.description: Full Linux distributions carry hundreds of packages the app never uses, each a potential CVE. Prefer minimal bases (distroless, Chainguard, Alpine, or -slim variants).
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: apt-get install without pinned versions
findings.description: Unpinned apt packages float across rebuilds, making images non-reproducible and silently pulling new versions. Pin versions: apt-get install pkg=1.2.3.
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.
